A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dynamic context cutoff work despite the changed title and format. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through readable text and visual inspection.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and the appendices report original QA, sufficiency detection, timing, classifier ablation and TREC in-context learning results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds comparative wall-clock measurements and experiments with synthetic sufficiency labels.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 retain attention-head probing, classifier ensembling, threshold-based prefix stopping, cached forward passes and the self-prompting alternative. The synthetic-label experiment changes training annotations without introducing a different cutoff algorithm or objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six single-hop and multi-hop datasets, including code understanding and key-value retrieval, their short/long context variants, and TREC in-context learning. Synthetic-label testing retains this coverage; summarization and other broader tasks are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The main QA and sufficiency comparator sets remain unchanged. V2 extends runtime comparisons beyond the full-context versus proposed-method curves in Figure 7: new Table 5 includes BM25, SBERT, all three LLMLingua variants, FT and self-prompting.

E3.justification: Appendix A replaces the reported 15,360/3,840/4,800 training/validation/test examples with 600 data points per dataset and an 80%/10%/10% split. V2 also introduces synthetic training labels evaluated against unchanged gold test labels and comparative seconds-per-sample measurements. The PDFs do not reconcile the sample-count descriptions or establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantial validation of dependence on human annotations through synthetic-versus-original label training (Appendix A.4), and practical efficiency through comparative latency/accuracy analysis (Section 4.3). The earlier threshold, chunking, head/ensemble, high-precision and TREC analyses remain.

E5.justification: Fivefold stratified cross-validation, existing distribution plots and dataset standard deviations are retained. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports inference times of 8.13 seconds for the proposed method, 9.02 for full context and 6.97 for LLMLingua2. New Table 8 reports synthetic/original-label F1 scores of 84.6/88.3 for 1B and 87.0/89.8 for 8B. These add latency and annotation-quality findings; the existing benchmark tables, appendix scores and plot contents remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The chunk/prefix definitions, sufficiency threshold, logistic probe, ensemble average and cached-forward-pass equations are equivalent. Removing duplicated formulation text and expanding caching explanations do not introduce a new proof, assumption or mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain internal sufficiency detection, dynamic cutoff, token savings and scale-dependent self-assessment. The headline changes from 1.3% to 3.4% accuracy improvement, but unchanged Table 2 means of 37.9 and 39.2 correspond to 1.3 percentage points or approximately 3.4% relative improvement, rather than a stronger underlying result.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive applicability discussion for summarization/rewriting and untested creative-writing/dialogue tasks, interprets synthetic labels as a route beyond explicit answer annotations, and discusses compatibility with KV-cache optimization. The new timing discussion also distinguishes practical latency/accuracy trade-offs among methods.

D1.justification: V2 expands label-construction instructions and reports an ensemble memory footprint below 15 MB with possible CPU offloading. Hardware and fine-tuning settings remain, while serving-framework and project-website disclosures disappear; the code link remains. New Appendix F.2 describes F1-based ensemble selection, conflicting with the retained AUC-based description.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around context reduction versus computational approximation, adding attention, KV-cache, quantization and speculative-decoding research. Positioning around latent activations expands to hallucination detection and reasoning verification, while several context-extension references are removed.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, extensively revises the introduction and related work, recasts dataset/baseline lists into paragraphs, removes the duplicated problem formulation, and reorganizes and expands the discussion and appendices. These constitute substantial editorial and structural revision.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the NeurIPS layout, restyles the title and headers, redraws Figure 2, repositions and resizes figures/tables, swaps Figures 5 and 6, and places the high-precision plots side by side. It also adds two result tables and an appendix contents page; retained plot images contain identical data.

improvement.justification: V2 improves evidential clarity through actual comparative runtimes, testing reliance on annotated sufficiency labels, clearer applicability limits and removal of duplicated text. These are useful gains, but unexplained dataset-size/split changes and conflicting ensemble-selection descriptions leave reproducibility concerns, limiting the overall improvement.
